name: b-flash-digicam-funfair
prompt: A candid night snapshot from a small travelling funfair on a damp town field around 2003, shot on a cheap pocket digital camera in its night-portrait mode, the built-in flash firing straight on while the shutter stays open a beat too long. Front and centre, filling the frame from mid-thigh up and seen from slightly below, stands a calm figure in a plain dark-red hand-knitted balaclava and matching woolly gloves, only the eyes visible through the two eye holes, the whole mask plain and evenly lit with no pattern on it. In one gloved hand it holds a huge cloud of bright pink candyfloss on a paper stick; from the other dangles a clear water-filled plastic bag with a single orange goldfish won at a hook-a-duck stall. It looks directly into the lens, perfectly still and politely unbothered, like a relative posing because someone said smile. The flash freezes the figure sharp, bright and slightly overexposed, with a hard small shadow falling behind it, while everything past arm's length drops away: the spinning waltzer cars and the bulb-studded rides behind smear into wobbly ribbons of magenta, lime, gold and electric blue, crossed with chunky jitters from a handheld long exposure, and the sky above is near-black and speckled with coarse colour noise. Punchy oversaturated early digital colour, a faintly cool white balance on the skin-free mask, mild purple fringing around the brightest bulbs, slight lens softness at the corners, a wonky snapshot framing as if taken by a laughing friend. No text, no lettering, no date stamp, no signs or logos anywhere in the frame. Thanks.
